newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM tells Fujimori he understands decision.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM tells Fujimori he understands decision.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Wednesday told Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori he understood his decision to send in troops to end a prolonged siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"I told President Fujimori that if I had been in his position I would have done the same," Hashimoto told a news conference after a brief conversation with Fujimori by telephone.
"I told him I understood his choice although I did inform him of my regret that we had no prior information," Hashimoto told his second news conference of the day.

"Thankfully, all Japanese nationals were rescued and those injured were only slightly hurt. But I offer condolences to the families of the one hostage and two soldiers who were killed in the operation."

In his first news conference soon after Peruvian troops stormed the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Hashimoto said he regretted he was not notified of the move beforehand but thanked the Peruvian government for the rescue operation.
In the telephone conversation, Fujimori told Hashimoto he could not give prior information to Japan because it was a "very delicate situation", Hashimoto said.
